name: 46,XY Difference of Sex Development Induced by Maternal Exposure to Endocrine Disruptors
aliases: Maternal Endocrine Disruptor-Associated 46,XY Disorder of Sex Development

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Endocrine Disruptor-Induced 46,XY DSD

criteria.description: Presence of 46,XY karyotype confirmed by chromosomal analysis
Documented maternal exposure to known endocrine-disrupting chemicals during pregnancy
Clinical evidence of ambiguous or undervirilized external genitalia at birth
Abnormal serum androgen and anti-Müllerian hormone levels inconsistent with typical male development
Ultrasound or MRI showing dysgenetic or absent internal male reproductive structures

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of 46,XY karyotype, documented maternal exposure to endocrine disruptors during pregnancy, and clinical evidence of ambiguous or undervirilized genitalia at birth
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of genetic mutations commonly associated with 46,XY DSD and other environmental causes.

pathognomonic.notes: Includes micropenis, hypospadias, and labioscrotal fusion abnormalities

common.symptomName: Reduced serum testosterone levels in neonatal period

searchTerms: late or missing male puberty changes
breast tissue growth in teenage boys

occasional.symptomName: Psychosocial distress related to gender ambiguity
searchTerms: emotional problems due to ambiguous genitalia

rare.symptomName: Renal anomalies such as unilateral renal agenesis

laboratory: Low serum testosterone and dihydrotestosterone levels in neonatal period
Elevated luteinizing hormone (LH) and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) levels
imaging: Ultrasound or MRI showing dysgenetic testes or absent Wolffian structures
Absence or hypoplasia of seminal vesicles
genetic: 46,XY karyotype without mutations in common DSD-associated genes (e.g., SRY, NR5A1, AR)
No pathogenic variants in androgen receptor or steroidogenic enzyme genes
other: Documented maternal exposure to endocrine-disrupting chemicals such as phthalates, bisphenol A, or pesticides during pregnancy

distinguishingFeatures: Complete androgen insensitivity presents with female external genitalia despite 46,XY karyotype
Normal or elevated serum testosterone levels
Normal male internal genitalia with undervirilized external genitalia

redFlags: Ambiguous genitalia detected at birth requiring urgent endocrinological evaluation
Severe undervirilization with salt-wasting or adrenal crisis signs
Rapid virilization in infancy or childhood suggesting alternative diagnosis
references: Hughes IA, et al. Consensus statement on management of intersex disorders. Arch Dis Child. 2006.
Lee PA, et al. Global DSD Update: Consensus on DSD nomenclature and classification. Horm Res Paediatr. 2016.
Diamanti-Kandarakis E, et al. Endocrine-disrupting chemicals: an Endocrine Society scientific statement. Endocr Rev. 2009.
